threats.abuse_case: A task reuses a revoked or expired capability to reach a service after its authority changed.
threats.mitigation: Capability tables carry revocation generations, leases, scope checks, and explicit rights projections.

threats.abuse_case: A component bypasses typed component ports or native kernel mediation to obtain ambient process authority.
threats.mitigation: The native syscall surface, service contracts, and userspace launch provenance reject unsigned or synthetic launch paths.

threats.abuse_case: A boot artifact, policy, driver set, or userspace image is modified after signing.
threats.mitigation: Measured boot records bind every artifact digest and QEMU negative profiles fail closed on tamper.

threats.abuse_case: A rollback, interrupted write, or crash recovery path loses persistent state or exposes unredacted diagnostics.
threats.mitigation: Recovery, storage durability, root-slot corruption, and crash record gates require deterministic recovery and redacted summaries.

threats.abuse_case: A service or app hides a sensitive action behind a stale policy decision or missing denial explanation.
threats.mitigation: Policy mediation, denial explanations, event ledger records, and permission review services record explicit decisions.

threats.abuse_case: Malformed storage logs, oversized payloads, or torn records corrupt object or workspace state.
threats.mitigation: Storage volume replay validates root slots, checksums, payload bounds, segment counts, and quota behavior.

threats.abuse_case: A remote node replays, duplicates, or redirects sync frames without a trusted platform root.
threats.mitigation: Device graph authorization, durable replay rejection and policy remain test backed. Noise XX channels certify fresh X25519 keys with graph-authenticated Ed25519 device identities rooted in an independent pin. Both QEMU guests decrypt remote traffic and reject tampering and replay. Directional keys, complete datagram-header authentication, a bounded replay bitmap, erasure and live trust rechecks protect the channel. The bounded object receiver independently checks locally bound capabilities, writable network shares and selective policy before staging, rejects stale version writes, erases revoked or expired transfers, and issues receipts only after durable checkpoints. The two-guest gate reloads a received object from the target disk before acknowledging it. Peer authentication requires a non-exportable sealed signing lease and retires traffic keys on lease expiry, revocation, policy denial or key changes. Vault catalog v3 atomically checkpoints graph enrollment, rotation and revocation with sealed keys and credentials; restore requires an independent root pin and verifies inner graph signatures before publishing state. Failed durable mutations block subsequent enrollment operations. The TPM guest gate generates all peer keys, commits enrollment and authenticates with the restored graph and sealed keys after reboot; only the separate public-pin enrollment anchor remains fixture signed. Rollback-resistant generation floors remain external. Runtime admission now bounds established peers to four sessions, two operations per dispatch, eight accepted frames per peer per tick and a 30-second lifetime. It rejects unknown peers before cryptography, preserves unrelated receive traffic, retries driver-backpressured ciphertext on deadlines without advancing nonces, and rechecks authority before every send. Inactive tasks, lost devices, expiry and revocation close channels and erase staging; the two-node gate verifies sync-task suspension cleanup. Receive slots are reclaimed independently of unread unrelated packets; an active protocol reservation partitions the unchanged 32-slot backing into eight peer and 24 generic slots, so either stalled consumer leaves the other capacity. A separate four-slot handshake table shares the existing dispatch budget with object traffic and accepts only locally selected device pairs with live sync-service and sealed-key authority. Ten-second lifetimes and per-tick receive limits bound pending work; retries reuse exact ciphertext and queued duplicates do not amplify responses. Failed authentication closes the attempt instead of allocating a replacement from network input. Host loss tests cover all Noise flights and both encrypted confirmations, while both QEMU guests verify pending-handshake cleanup on task suspension. Final confirmation bytes survive successful handoff so application retries can recover a lost last delivery. The runtime sender independently binds a local read capability, network share and selective policy, pins source version and blob identity, and rechecks them before reads and cached egress. It streams bounded storage ranges without a second plaintext snapshot, pins the first authenticated destination offer, and rejects unsent-range or premature durable receipts. Lost application replies trigger fresh-nonce retries of idempotent requests; driver backpressure retains exact ciphertext. Host tests drop each object protocol leg and cover source edits, scope denial, revocation, failed durable barriers and invalid receipts; both QEMU guests use runtime sessions and prove sender and receiver retirement. Service-owned connections now replace borrowed transfer state with four generation-checked handles. Only authorized local opens allocate bounded coordination and receive bytes. Handoff rechecks authority and source version within the existing dispatch budget; release, expiry, authentication failure or task retirement removes protocol pointers before scrubbing and freeing allocations. Handle generations survive reset and never wrap. Tests cover stale handles, capacity, loss across handoff, changed authority and promotion failure without damaging another session. The two-node proof retires pending owners on storage suspension and active owners on sync suspension. Production identity provisioning, discovery and connection provisioning, continuous convergence and typed secret/collection/event-stream protocols remain release blockers.

threats.abuse_case: Crash dumps or support bundles include secrets, capability tokens, raw memory, or private object names by default.
threats.mitigation: Crash summaries redact sensitive reason strings and the release policy denies raw memory capture by default.

threats.abuse_case: A restarted userspace driver keeps stale broker authority, DMA metadata, or port access.
threats.mitigation: Driver restart proofs reject stale authority, stale DMA/port access, and rebind fresh broker sessions by generation.
